header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - Echo Analytics), Tom Reynolds (AI Platform Lead), Sara Kim (Security), Ben Ortiz (ML Eng), plus 1 muted attendee
Meeting notes: discovery call focused on migrating from OpenAI hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated / Private, compatibility with vLLM and TGI stacks, eval parity concerns, and security/compliance questions.
summary: Echo Analytics is evaluating migrating majority of their inference from OpenAI to either Redwood Hosted or Dedicated. Primary drivers: cost predictability, lower latency for internal workflows, and data residency. Key concerns: API compatibility, parity with current vLLM/TGI microservices, model weights licensing, and security (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed to run an eval/benchmark (POC) against Echo's corpus and measure latency/cost/quality parity. Next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we're Maya (AE) and Ravi and Lina from Redwood. How's everyone?
[00:07] Priya Nair: Hey Maya, thanks. Quick intro — I'm Priya, CTO at Echo Analytics. We run a mix of hosted OpenAI for prod and some on-prem vLLM for high-volume internal tasks.
[00:14] Tom Reynolds: Tom here, lead the platform. We're looking at migrating to a dedicated provider, want cost predictability and faster tail latencies.
[00:21] Maya Chen: Great context. Today's goal is to understand your workload, constraints, and what success looks like. We'll also talk compatibility — I know you mentioned vLLM and TGI — and outline a POC.
[00:34] Ben Ortiz: Quick note, we have a custom TGI-based microservice for chat summarization; it uses quantized weights and KV cache. 
[00:42] Lina Gomez: Perfect, that helps. Can you share current RPS, typical sequence lengths, and models you're using?
[00:49] Tom Reynolds: Sure — at peak we do about 120 qps across features, average seq len around 600 tokens for summarization, 150 tokens for QA. Mostly using OpenAI gpt-4o and some Anthropic for sensitive content.
[01:03] Ravi Patel: Thanks. A few quick clarifying Qs: when you say Anthropic, is that for a particular workload or red team safety checks?
[01:08] Tom Reynolds: Mostly safety-sensitive assistant flows. For batch internal jobs we spin up vLLM with 4-bit quantized models; it's cheaper but higher maintenance.
[01:18] Priya Nair: Our goals are threefold: 1) reduce per-token spend by ~30% over OpenAI, 2) have predictable capacity for peak hours, 3) keep data in-region (EU for some customers).
[01:31] Maya Chen: Ok. Sounds like Redwood Dedicated or Private could be a fit — Dedicated for reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput, Private for full VPC + data controls. Quick question on model licensing — do you use any vendor-restricted weights today?
[01:43] Ben Ortiz: No, we primarily use open models and fine-tuned variants; some internal finetunes on Llama2-family and a few Bloom-like models.
[01:52] Ravi Patel: Good, that simplifies onboarding. On the compatibility front, Redwood exposes our REST/SDKs; for vLLM/TGI parity we can support the same model artifacts and runtime paths, but there are nuanced behavior differences — e.g., tokenization variations and decoding defaults.
[02:08] Tom Reynolds: That's one of our concerns — eval parity. We have a regression test set and want to ensure outputs don't drift. How do you handle model parity and eval drift?
[02:16] Lina Gomez: We do two things: 1) we run side-by-side evals on your corpus during the POC and report per-example diffs, and 2) we expose model version pinning so your rollout can be gradual. We also provide determinism knobs — sampling seeds, temperature settings, and tokenizer config alignment.
[02:29] Sara Kim: From security side, we need SOC 2 Type II, KMS integration, SSO/SAML, and audit logs. Also, network diagram for Dedicated setup.
[02:38] Maya Chen: Yep, we have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. We'll send the network diagram.
[02:44] Priya Nair: For Private deployments, is there an air-gapped option? Some clients require it.
[02:48] Ravi Patel: We offer an on-prem package. It requires a little more integration work but supports air-gapped and HSM/KMS options.
[02:54] Tom Reynolds: Latency question — our internal vLLM has sub-100ms 95th for short prompts, OpenAI is variable. Can Redwood hit that on Dedicated?
[03:02] Lina Gomez: On Dedicated with the right instance types and batching config, sub-100ms 95th for short prompts is achievable. For longer sequences KV cache and attention kernel selection help keep cost down. We'll recommend instance sizing during the POC.
[03:14] Ben Ortiz: How do we handle our TGI microservice migration? It's a custom stack referencing model file layouts and certain environment flags.
[03:21] Ravi Patel: We can support the same model file types; we have a migration guide for TGI and vLLM users that maps config flags to Redwood runtime params. Some flags don't have one-to-one mappings, so we'll do a compatibility run as part of the POC.
[03:36] Priya Nair: Pricing — curious about Reserved vs on-demand. We want a committed model to hit cost targets.
[03:41] Maya Chen: Dedicated has monthly reserved tiers with commit discounts; we can model your expected qps and token volume and show committed vs burst costs. I'll send the pricing grid after this call.
[03:50] Tom Reynolds: For the eval we'll need to run against our test harness — is there a sandbox cluster or one-off Dedicated node we can use?
[03:57] Lina Gomez: We can provision a temporary Dedicated pool for the POC or give you access to a hosted sandbox with similar kernels. For strict parity we'd recommend the Dedicated pool to match production.
[04:08] Sara Kim: On auditability, how granular are logs? We need request/response logs redacted per policy and admin audit trails.
[04:16] Ravi Patel: We log token-level metrics, latencies, and request metadata. Full request/response can be configured to be retained short-term or forwarded to your logging endpoint with redaction rules.
[04:27] Priya Nair: Ok good. About model fine-tunes — we have internal finetunes that include PII in training data. How do you isolate that when transferring weights?
[04:36] Maya Chen: For Dedicated/Private, weights stay in your control; you can stage them in your S3 and we pull via temporary, scoped credentials. For Private/on-prem it's fully customer-managed.
[04:45] Ben Ortiz: When you say "pull weights" do you support s3-compatible endpoints or only AWS?
[04:49] Lina Gomez: We support S3-compatible endpoints and signed URLs. We'll include details in the POC checklist.
[04:57] Tom Reynolds: Regarding model behavior differences, if we see regression on a small percent of examples, what's the rollback path?
[05:03] Ravi Patel: We recommend pinning a canary percentage, run canary traffic, and rollback to the pinned model. We also keep previous model artifacts so we can route traffic back within minutes.
[05:12] Priya Nair: Timeframe — we want to decide in 3 weeks, pilot in month after. Is that realistic?
[05:18] Maya Chen: Yes. Typical discovery -> POC -> pilot is 4-8 weeks depending on complexity. For your case, with open models and existing infra, 4-6 weeks is doable.
[05:27] Ben Ortiz: One more — do you support GPU types A100 vs H100 choices? We have perf differences between them.
[05:33] Lina Gomez: Yes, Dedicated supports A100 and H100 pools; we can test both during benchmarks. H100 often gives better throughput on certain model families.
[05:40] Tom Reynolds: Great. For the POC what metrics will you collect?
[05:44] Ravi Patel: We'll collect latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), throughput, tokenized cost estimates, and output diffs vs your baseline. We'll produce a report with charts.
[05:54] Priya Nair: On the output diffs, can you show semantic similarity scores and human-reviewed regressions?
[05:59] Lina Gomez: Yes, we can run automated semantic similarity (embedding cosine) and flag top regressions for manual review.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Ok, logistics: Maya will send pricing and security package; Ravi will propose bench config; Tom to share corpus and peak qps; Sara to send compliance questionnaire.
[06:18] Tom Reynolds: We'll also share our TGI config repo — might be helpful.
[06:23] Ben Ortiz: Expect some rough edges in the TGI configs, we didn't standardize env flags.
[06:28] Priya Nair: Any known limitations we should be aware of?
[06:31] Ravi Patel: A couple: model tokenizer differences can cause small generation deltas; quantization modes may vary across runtimes affecting perf/quality tradeoffs; and some edge-case ops in custom finetunes may need small recoding.
[06:44] Tom Reynolds: Noted. On the contract side, what's the minimum commitment?
[06:49] Maya Chen: Dedicated monthly minimum is typically a 3-month commitment for POC pools, enterprise reserved plans vary. We'll include an example contract template with pricing.
[06:58] Sara Kim: On SSO — do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[07:02] Lina Gomez: Yes, SAML + SCIM supported for Redwood Console and RBAC.
[07:08] Priya Nair: Any third-party SOC references?
[07:11] Maya Chen: We can include auditors and evidence in the pack.
[07:15] Tom Reynolds: Ok let's talk timeline again — we want the benchmark next week, is that doable?
[07:19] Ravi Patel: We can run an initial smoke benchmark next week if you share the corpus mid-week; full POC with multiple configs would take 1-2 weeks.
[07:29] Ben Ortiz: We'll aim to send corpus by Tuesday.
[07:33] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll follow up with the pricing and the POC checklist today.
[07:38] Priya Nair: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[07:41] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Quick recap in chat and action items captured.
[07:45] [call ends]
